9	SilverBullet [[Space|spaces]] are scriptable environments. This is where a lot of SilverBullet’s power and flexibility comes from. This page lays out the trust model that follows from that, so you can configure a deployment that matches who you’re sharing it with. For a more basic walk-through of concrete setups, see [[Security Profiles]].
10	
11	You need to trust people with `write` access. Anyone who can write to a space can author [[Space Lua]] and other dynamic content that runs in the browser of anyone who later opens that space.
12	
13	# Access levels
14	Each space resolves to one of three [[Dashboard#Access|access levels]] for a given visitor, plus a separate admin flag:
15	
16	* **`none`:** Not visible. Requests are refused.
17	* **`read`:** May view content, will run all scripts and queries locally. Cannot modify anything or reach any capability endpoint.
18	* **`write`:** Full access to the space’s content **and** capabilities.
19	
20	Admins get `write` on every space, plus the `/.dashboard` management UI.
21	
22	# What `write` really means
23	`write` is not just “can edit files” in the narrow sense — a `write` member can create content that runs, unattended, as whoever else opens that space. That includes admins.
24	
25	The practical rule: **grant `write` only to people you’d trust to act as any member of every space they can reach.** If someone doesn’t clear that bar, don’t add them as a `write` member of a space other trusted people also use, give them their own space, on its own (sub)domain instead (see [[Security Profiles#Software team]]). SilverBullet does not offer an in-between “can edit, but can’t script” role within a single space.
26	
27	# Capability endpoints
28	A few endpoints can reach beyond the space’s own content, and all require `write`:
29	
30	* **Shell** (`/.shell`) — runs any command on the server. (Off by default)
31	* **HTTP proxy** (`/.proxy`, exposed to Lua as [[API/net#net.proxyFetch(url, options?)|net.proxyFetch]]) — fetches an external URL through the server, on the server’s network.
32	* **Runtime API** (`/.runtime`) — evaluates Lua and scripts via a headless browser instance, see [[Runtime API]].
33

60	* `POST /.revisions/`: Commits everything outstanding immediately. Takes no body, returns `{"committed": true|false}`. Returns `409` for a space that is not in Managed mode.
61	* `GET /.revisions/?rev=<hash>&to=<hash|HEAD|WORKING>`: A summary of everything that changed between `rev` and `to` as JSON: `from`, `to`, `files` (each with `path`, `status`, `added` and `removed`) and `authors`. `to=WORKING` reaches all the way to what’s on disk, uncommitted changes included.
62	* `GET /.revisions/<path>`: One file’s revisions as JSON: `mode`, `uncommitted` (whether what is on disk differs from the last commit), `revisions` and `more`. Takes the same `before`/`limit` parameters.
63	* `GET /.revisions/<path>?rev=<hash>`: The content of that file as it was at that revision, served with the file’s own content type.
64	* `GET /.revisions/<path>?rev=<hash>&format=diff`: A unified diff of what that revision changed in that file, as `text/plain`. `404` when the revision has nothing to diff against a parent (a merge commit).
65	* `GET /.revisions/<path>?format=diff`: With no `rev`, the *uncommitted* change instead — HEAD versus what is on disk, as `text/plain`. A file that has never been committed reads as wholly added. `404` when it matches HEAD after all.
66	
67	# Search
68	The server answers [[Search]] itself, so these work without the [[Runtime API]]. The [[CLI]]’s `sb search` and `sb related` use them. They need Read access. Public visitors only get the modes the server allows them, and no related pages. Bodies are JSON. Errors are 4xx JSON with an `error` code and a `message`.
69	
70	* `GET /.search/status`: What search can do right now: `backend` (`null` when unavailable), `model`, `capabilities` (`modes`, the first being the default, and whether `related` is available), `ready`, `progress` (`{"done", "total"}` while building) and `reason`.
71	* `POST /.search/query`: Body `{"query", "mode", "scope", "include", "exclude", "limit"}`. Only `query` is required. `mode` is `words`, `phrase` or `natural` (the **Semantic** mode), `scope` is `pages`, `meta` or `all`, `limit` is at most 50. Returns `items` (matches, best page first, each with `page`, `pos`, `line`, `heading`, `excerpt` and `highlights`), `total`, `partial` and `notice` (e.g. when semantic search fell back to word matching). With `X-Await-Index: 1`, a member’s query first lets the index catch up with recent file changes and the response carries `X-Index-Status`, as described in [[Runtime API#Waiting for the index]].
72	* `POST /.search/related`: Body `{"page", "limit", "exclude", "scope"}`: pages related in meaning to `page`, in the same shape as a query’s result. Needs semantic search.
73	
74	# Help
75	`GET /.help`: What an assistant needs to start working in the space, as JSON with `"version": 1`: the skills available (pages tagged `meta/skill`: the built-in `Library/Std` ones, those of installed libraries and the space’s own, each with its page, description and source), an `outline` of the space (`folders` with page counts, a capped list of top-level `pages` with `pageCount`, whether an `AGENTS` page exists, and the `tags` and attributes used in page frontmatter), and `runtime`, whether the [[Runtime API]] is available to the caller. The [[CLI]]’s `sb help` and the [[MCP]]’s `help` tool render it. It needs a signed-in account or an API token, even on a public space: anonymous visitors get `401` (or the sign-in redirect), although they can read `/.fs`. While the space’s first scan is still running, `scanning` is true and only the built-in skills are listed.
76	
77	# RPC
78	Some functionality is exposed as RPC-style calls
79	
80	* `GET /.ping`: Returns 200 with body `OK` if the server is available.
81	* `POST /.shell`: Run a shell command on the server side and return the result.
82	* `POST /.logs`: Accepts a JSON array of log entry objects with fields `source`, `level`, `message`, and `timestamp`. The server logs these with the client’s IP. Returns `OK`.
83	* `* /.proxy/<host[:port]>/path`: Proxy an HTTP request to avoid CORS issues.
84	  * Blocked in read-only mode (returns 405).
85	  * The URI does not include a scheme — it is auto-detected: `http://` is used for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, bare IP addresses, and `host.docker.internal`. `https://` is used for everything else.
86	  * Request headers prefixed with `X-Proxy-Header-` have the prefix stripped and are forwarded to the upstream server.
87	  * Upstream response headers are returned with an `x-proxy-header-` prefix.
88	  * The `x-proxy-status-code` header contains the actual upstream HTTP status code. The proxy response itself always returns 200 to avoid interference.
89	
90	## Runtime API
91	Enabled when Chrome/Chromium is available and runtime access is permitted. In single-space mode, `SB_RUNTIME_API=0` disables it. In multi-space mode, use the administrator’s APIs controls and per-writer Runtime API permission. See [[Runtime API]] for full documentation, setup instructions, and examples.
92	
93	## MCP
94	In [[Dashboard|multi-space mode]], `POST /.mcp` is a stateless [[MCP]] (Model Context Protocol) endpoint that authenticates with an OAuth access token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`, issued to a connected app); API tokens are refused with `401` and a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge pointing at the resource metadata. These endpoints are served on the main router only in multi-space mode, answer `404` unless an admin has turned MCP on (it is off by default) and when `SB_MCP=0` (except `/.auth/revoke`), and are not served in single-space mode:
95	
96	* `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/.mcp` (also at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`): RFC 9728 resource metadata.
97	* `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`: RFC 8414 authorization server metadata.
98	* `POST /.auth/register`: RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, answers `201`. Registered clients are public (`token_endpoint_auth_method` `none`).
99	* `GET /.auth/mcp/authorize`: authorization endpoint (PKCE). Signed-out requests redirect to the Dashboard login; the consent page lists the spaces to grant.
